objective.primary: Make the Cognitive Biases knowledge library easy for people, search systems and AI agents to identify, retrieve, verify and cite while preserving evidence status, research maturity and the distinction between a useful decision lens and a psychological diagnosis.
targetQuestions: What is a cognitive bias and how should it be used as a decision lens?
What evidence supports or limits a named cognitive bias?
Which cognitive biases are relevant to a real decision when the bias name is not known?
How can an AI assistant use cognitive-bias evidence without diagnosing a person?
What human-AI decision effects are being studied by this project and what is their maturity?
How can AI models be tested for sensitivity to controlled decision conditions?
What does the Cognitive Bias Observatory measure and what does it not measure?
How can builders reuse the public Cognitive Biases dataset reproducibly?

answerPages.description: Publish situation-first and question-first pages that route a reader from a real decision to a small set of reviewed lenses instead of forcing them to know a bias name first.

originalResearch.description: Publish preregistered protocols, research notes, experiment specifications, benchmark methods and evidence updates with explicit maturity and limitations.

protocolObservatory.description: The ARWP protocol-observatory module tracks agentic-web protocols; this project instead maintains a cognitive-bias information observatory and does not duplicate ARWP protocol research.

comparisonPages.description: Publish reviewed comparisons that distinguish easily confused concepts and route agents to the narrower explanation when labels overlap.

conceptDefinitions.description: Maintain canonical concept pages with explicit entry kinds, evidence state, related concepts and practical interpretation boundaries.

claimsRegistry.description: Promote a small subset of important evidence-sensitive project claims to stable claim identifiers only when the existing provenance model can support scoped review and supersession without duplicating the evidence database.

evidenceReceipts.description: Create compact replayable receipts for selected research and benchmark outputs when they add value beyond the existing release manifest, checksums and provenance records.

crawlerMatrix.description: Document site-specific AI/search crawler policy only from official crawler documentation and deployed robots behavior; do not infer training or retrieval behavior from user-agent names alone.

agentFetchLab.description: Test which Cognitive Biases surfaces assistants and agents actually retrieve for representative questions before optimizing around assumed discovery behavior.

knowledgeGraph.description: Expose a compact JSON-LD graph connecting the website, maintainer organization, public dataset, research program, benchmark, observatory and trust surface.

citationVisuals.description: Publish selected evidence and research visuals with stable URLs, source notes and accessible descriptions when the visual materially improves understanding or citation.

openReuseAssets.description: The project currently uses CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 content terms and does not claim the permission-free CC BY media profile used by ARWP; reuse must follow the repository licence.

trustCenter.description: Publish one canonical trust surface covering identity, evidence and review practices, provenance, security reporting, licence boundaries and known limitations.

correctionsLedger.description: Maintain a public corrections policy and machine-readable ledger for material factual, evidence, provenance, methodology or data-contract errors.

softwareProvenance.description: Add verifiable build or artifact provenance only for software artifacts that are actually distributed and consumed; do not treat ordinary Pages deployment as a security attestation.

persistentIdentifiers.description: Use a DOI or another externally issued persistent identifier for dataset or research releases only after issuance; repository citation metadata alone is not a DOI.

externalTrustSignals.description: Expose independent repository or archival trust signals only after they have actually run or been issued, and keep their scope separate from scientific correctness.

externalDistribution.description: Create externally distributed references for substantial evidence or research releases while keeping the canonical site and versioned dataset as the source of record.

aiVisibility.description: Measure observable AI citations, grounding queries and referrals separately from search visibility, without turning them into a single readiness or authority score.

localization.description: Expose canonical English semantics plus German and Russian discovery-routing surfaces for AI agents with deterministic English fallback; this does not claim full human-interface translation.

history.description: Expose source-backed project evolution and current maturity as both a human-readable timeline and machine-readable JSON.

vocabulary.definition: A compact task-specific workflow that uses a small set of relevant cognitive-bias or decision-science lenses as checking questions rather than as diagnoses or scores.
A project research layer for studying human-AI decision effects while preserving explicit maturity states and preferring established concepts when they already explain an observation.
A public descriptive observation layer for headline-level framing, certainty, salience, authority, social-proof, numerical and repetition signals with explicit sampling limits.

signals.name: search visibility
signals.description: Track canonical-page indexing and search performance through available webmaster tooling without treating visibility changes as proof that a content or ARWP change caused ranking gains.

signals.name: AI citations and referrals
signals.description: Track observable citations, grounding references and referrals where platforms expose them, keeping platform coverage and query sampling explicit.

signals.name: external references
signals.description: Track external links or references to the dataset, evidence reviews, research artifacts and project-defined decision tools without converting them into an authority score.

measurement.privacy: Use aggregate, privacy-minimized visibility signals. Do not turn decision-tool drafts, MCP queries or visitor activity into a browsing-history or psychological-profile dataset.
